comments.text: If you enjoyed this video, leave a like 👍 and subscribe. It helps the video reach a wider audience and allows us to keep uncovering more hidden stories from across Canada.

comments.author: @tonydamiani7353
comments.text: 99.9% of everything that ever existed on earth is now extinct. It's called evolution.

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: That 99.9% figure is a commonly cited estimate, but extinction and evolution aren’t quite the same thing. Species disappear for all kinds of reasons, climate shifts, competition, habitat change, catastrophes, and sometimes human activity. This video is specifically about the Canadian populations and species whose losses we can actually trace historically. 👍

comments.author: @chaseolson4008
comments.text: Mustella Nigripes - black footed ferret are being raised by my hometown in montana. They struggle to expand into their native territories because of a lack of prairie dogs

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: That’s really interesting, especially having a recovery program that close to home. Their dependence on prairie dogs is such a huge bottleneck, you can raise ferrets successfully, but without enough healthy prairie dog colonies there’s nowhere for them to really expand. Thanks for adding the local perspective!

comments.author: @chaseolson4008
comments.text: Those greater prairie grouse are super rare in Montana now. They've been declining all my life

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: Yeah, that decline is hard to watch. Greater prairie-chickens need such specific grassland habitat that once it gets fragmented, recovery gets really difficult. Hopefully the remaining Montana populations can hang on.

replies.author: @pandastylearmy5938
replies.text: @HiddenCanada i like you. you have class.

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: You’re absolutely right that elk live in Canada today, and wolves have been seen again in Newfoundland. The distinction in the video is the original eastern elk population and the extinct Newfoundland wolf subspecies. Ontario’s current elk were reintroduced from western Canadian stock, and the wolves confirmed in Newfoundland in recent years have tested as Labrador wolves, not descendants of the old island population. Easy detail to miss, though, appreciate you watching! 👍
